title: Type 2 immune history trains lung macrophages for viral disease tolerance.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Found two GEO series (gene expression archive) by title search, since the paper has no PMCID and NCBI elink returned nothing: GSE343897 (14 samples: 6 bulk exon-count files, 4 single-cell RNA-seq lanes with 169-198 MB matrices, 4 sample-tag reference CSVs) and GSE280183 (8 ATAC-seq peak files, 4 steady-state vs 4 trained NAM (nerve- and airway-associated macrophage) samples). I opened one peak file (110,803 peaks, GRCm38 mouse genome coordinates, MACS2 narrowPeak format), one bulk exon-count file (406,855 exon rows keyed by Ensembl gene:exon) and one sample-tag reference (CMO301-303 tags labelled 'Naive').
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The experimental design (Nippostrongylus-conditioned vs unconditioned mice, influenza challenge, survival, NAM depletion and transfer) and the human lung atlas meta-analysis come from the abstract only. No full text, no supplement and no Zenodo record were found.

a1_downloadable.note: Both GEO series are public; filelists fetched and small files downloaded without login.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No label column exists. A trained-vs-naive label per peak or per gene would have to be built by differential analysis across 4 vs 4 ATAC samples or 3 vs 3 bulk samples (verified file listing).

a3_inputs_present.note: Peaks carry genomic coordinates (sequence retrievable from the mm10 reference); counts carry Ensembl IDs.

a4_units_stated.note: Raw counts and MACS2 peak scores; standard formats, units implicit but conventional.

a5_enough_rows.note: The independent unit is the mouse sample: 8 ATAC samples, 6 bulk RNA samples, 4 multiplexed single-cell lanes. Peak or cell counts are large but are not independent labelled examples.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~21 MB peaks, ~9 MB bulk counts, ~615 MB single-cell matrices
a6_fits_laptop.note: Fits; the single-cell matrices exceed the 50 MB per-file cap and were not downloaded.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No full text to compare; GEO sample counts are internally consistent.

a8_label_provenance.note: Any per-peak label would be a differential-accessibility call computed from the same peak signals used as features, so it is derived, not measured.

honest_claim_h3: At best a model could separate chromatin regions that were more open in trained versus naive lung macrophages in 4 versus 4 mice from one lab, which is a differential-analysis result, not a prediction task.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA sequence of open-chromatin regions to predict which regions become more open after prior worm infection in lung macrophages.
plain_idea.train_on: About 110,000 open-chromatin regions per sample (verified in one file), from 8 mouse samples total.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a region gains accessibility in trained macrophages; the answer would have to be computed by comparing 4 trained against 4 naive ATAC-seq (chromatin accessibility sequencing) samples.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Immunologists studying trained immunity might learn which transcription-factor motifs mark the trained state, but the paper already names the IL-4-STAT6-PPARgamma program.

ml_idea: Sequence-to-differential-accessibility classifier on NAM ATAC peaks; rejected because the label is constructed from 4 vs 4 samples and the effective n is the mouse.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; project rejected at Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count independent labelled units: 8 ATAC samples and 6 bulk samples, already done.

verdict_reason: Mechanistic mouse immunology study with 8 ATAC-seq and 6 bulk RNA-seq samples and no outcome column; any label must be built by differential analysis of the same data (A2, A5, A8 fail).
